title: Telemetry resharding & storage retention playbook (VPC/on-prem)
content:
Purpose:
This working playbook captures a pragmatic plan for resharding metric ingestion, rolling out stricter retention policies, and the Terraform module changes we need when operating Prometheus/Grafana + Thanos/remote storage inside customer VPCs or on-prem clusters. It focuses on minimizing data loss risk, avoiding alert storms, and giving SREs predictable rollback paths.

Context / rationale:
- Some customers (large enterprise, regulated) have tight retention + storage constraints. We need to support shorter hot-block retention, longer cold-storage TTL, and re-sharding when ingest QPS increases.
- Current private-deploy stacks vary (k8s flavors, S3-compatible object stores, limited node storage). Our terraform modules have to be more opinionated about block storage and compaction config.

High-level goals:
1) Define a safe resharding process for Prometheus TSDB when moving from single-replica ingestion to multi-replica + remote_write into Thanos/obj store.
2) Add Terraform variables and module patterns to make retention and compaction configurable per-customer.
3) Provide a step-by-step upgrade and smoke-test plan (canary namespaces, key metrics, rollback hooks).
4) Document alerts and throttling knobs to prevent system overload during migrations.

Assumptions / constraints:
- Customer clusters may not allow disruptive node restarts during business hours.
- Some object stores are S3-compatible but lack strong consistency guarantees.
- We cannot assume uniform Prometheus operator versions across deployments.

Quick TL;DR checklist (ops):
- [ ] Preflight: collect current TSDB block sizes, retention, current remote_write config (if any), disk utilization, and ingestion QPS (5m/1h).
- [ ] Convert a small set of tenants/namespaces to remote_write -> Thanos receive in a canary VPC/namespace.
- [ ] Validate queries and alerts against canary data for 48–72h.
- [ ] Reshard: scale up receiver *and* add new ruler/compactor replicas as needed.
- [ ] Cutover remaining namespaces in waves (configured in TF as "waves").
- [ ] Post-cutover: increase retention TTL in object store + run offline compaction if required.

Prometheus / Thanos notes (technical):
- Minimum tested versions: Prometheus 2.45+, Thanos 0.35+.
- Recommended architecture inside VPC: prometheus (per-namespace) -> remote_write -> thanos-receiver (ingest) -> object store (S3/GCS/minio) + compactor + store-gateway.
- If the customer has limited disk, set local retention to 24–72h and rely on remote_write for longer queries.
- Use HA receive model: at least 3 replicas for receiver and compactor in production for resilience.

Terraform module changes (sketch):
- New module: modules/telemetry/remote_storage
  - variables:
    - object_store_type (string) e.g. s3 | s3-compatible | gcs
    - retention_days (number) // remote retention target
    - local_retention_seconds (number) // prometheus flag
    - reshard_waves (list(string)) // namespace groups for rolling cutover
    - enable_thanos_receive (bool)
    - instance_class / vm_size (string)
  - outputs:
    - thanos_endpoint_url
    - object_store_bucket

- Example usage snippet (pseudocode):
  module "telemetry" {
    source = "git::ssh://git@github.com/redwood-inference/infra.git//modules/telemetry?ref=main"
    object_store_type = "s3-compatible"
    retention_days = 365
    local_retention_seconds = 172800  // 48h
    reshard_waves = ["canary", "wave-1", "wave-2"]
  }

Important tf variable semantics:
- Changing local_retention_seconds in-place is fine (prom flags will update via daemonset rolling restart).
- Enabling thanos_receive requires creating persistent volumes and should be treated as "stateful" — manual confirmation required before apply.
- Object store credentials must be provided as KMS-wrapped secrets; terraform will create secret objects and never write raw keys to state (use kms_provider = "customer-managed" option).

Upgrade + cutover plan (detailed):
Phase 0 — Preflight (2–7 days)
- Gather metrics: disk_used_bytes, prometheus_target_sync_total, remote_write_errors_total, ingestion_rate (samples/second).
- Backup: take snapshot of Prometheus TSDB blocks (prometheus snapshot CLI) for the top-5 namespaces by disk usage. Store snapshots in object store prefix snapshots/<date>/<ns>/
- Validate object store connectivity and permissions.
- Run terraform plan with dry-run to see the resources that will change.
- Create rollback runbooks and Slack incident channel.

Phase 1 — Canary (48–72h)
- Pick low-risk namespace and a canary customer.
- Deploy Thanos receive and configure remote_write only for the canary namespace (modify prometheus CR for that namespace).
- Observe: remote_write_dropped_samples_total, thanos_receive_receive_requests_total, compactor_blocks_compacted_total.
- Check query latency (Grafana synthetic panel) for range queries that span remote storage.
- If issues: revert prometheus CR to previous remote_write config (small rolling restart), and restore snapshot if data missing.

Phase 2 — Wave-based rollout (days depending on scale)
- For each wave in reshard_waves:
  - Apply terraform to move wave to remote_write -> thanos.
  - Wait 24–48h while monitoring the following:
    - prom_disk_usage (should slowly drop)
    - remote_write_queue_length (should be small)
    - receiver_cpu/memory (should be under thresholds)
    - alert flood detection: high rate of alert firing in last 30m -> pause rollout.

Phase 3 — Post-cutover maintenance (48–96h)
- Run compactor manual run if blocks need rewriting to save space.
- Tweak compaction retention and downsampling.
- Increase remote retention TTL in object store lifecycle policy.

Rollback strategy:
- For remote_write problems: revert Prometheus CR to remove remote_write and restart pods (data will be local again if retention not expired).
- For object-store corruption: use snapshots to rehydrate top namespaces.
- Terraform-level rollback: use tf state rollback to previous commit and re-apply. Keep old statefile snapshot before big changes.

Smoke tests and validation (automated):
- Query test suite: run a set of historical queries (5m, 1h, 24h windows) and compare results between pre-cutover baseline and post-cutover. Allow small gaps for downsampled series.
- Alert test: synthesize test metrics to trigger a canary alert and verify playbook run.
- Load test: replay ingestion at 1.5x typical QPS against thanos-receiver in staging.

Prometheus operator / CRD migration notes:
- If CRD changes are required, perform CRD update during a low-impact window. New CRDs may require the operator to restart and reconcile all Prometheus objects.
- Avoid upgrading operator + enabling thanos_receive in the same wave. Split into separate TF commits.

OTEL collector / logs shipping considerations:
- OTEL Collector may be used for logs -> Kafka/S3. If using kafka: ensure topic partition counts align with receiver shard count to avoid reordering/backpressure.
- For log-heavy customers, consider a separate ingress path: logs -> fluentd/fluency -> kafka -> long-term store. Do not overload prometheus nodes with logs agent indexing.

Alert and throttling rules to add before cutover (examples):
- Alert: "TelemetryReceiverBackpressure" when remote_write_queue_length > 5000 for > 10m. Severity: high.
- Alert: "PrometheusDiskPressure" when disk_utilization > 80% for > 15m. Severity: critical.
- Add autoscaler policy templates for thanos-receive deployment CPU.

Open questions / decisions to resolve:
- Should we offer a managed config for compactor downsampling levels (e.g., 15s->1m->5m) per customer or keep a global setting? (Ops / Product tradeoff)
- For S3-compatible stores with eventual consistency, do we add delayed compaction windows or strict write-confirmation checks?
- Policy: default local retention for private deployments: 48h vs 72h? (Ops lean 48h, SRE suggests 72h)

TODOs (owner assignments):
- Aisha: add terraform module tests and example for minio + thanos in infra repo (PR target: infra/modules/telemetry). (due 2025-01-15)
- Liam: draft Grafana dashboards for migration observability (panels: remote_write_errors, receiver_lag, query_latency). (due 2024-12-01)
- Priya: add alert runbook entries for TelemetryReceiverBackpressure and PrometheusDiskPressure. (due 2024-12-15)

Notes-to-self / rough commands:
- Take prometheus snapshot: kubectl exec -n <ns> $(kubectl get po -n <ns> -l app=prometheus -o name | head -n1) -- prometheus snapshot 
- Example remote_write snippet for prometheus CR: 
  remote_write:
    - url: http://thanos-receiver.<svc-namespace>.svc.cluster.local:19291/api/v1/receive
      sigv4: {} # if using AWS IAM
      queue_config:
        max_samples_per_send: 1000
        capacity: 25000

- Terraform plan tips: run with TF_LOG=info for provider details; run plan with -target for canary wave first.

Appendix: quick compatibility matrix (working)
- Prometheus <2.41: may lack some relabel_config features we need -> require operator upgrade.
- Prometheus 2.41–2.45: supported for simple remote_write.
- Thanos <0.30: not recommended (missing receive HA features).

End of draft notes — this doc is intentionally iterative. Use it as a base for an RFC or a more formal runbook once the canary completes.

Revision history:
- 2024-11-10: initial draft (Aisha)
- 2024-12-03: added TF variable semantics and early TODOs (Liam)
